claims: The Artemis II mission uses liquid hydrogen (LH2) as fuel for its Space Launch System (SLS) rocket core stage.
The Artemis II mission uses liquid oxygen (LOX) as the oxidizer for its Space Launch System (SLS) rocket core stage.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) uses LH2.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) uses LOX.
The two solid rocket boosters utilize Ammonium Perchlorate Composite Propellant (APCP).
The rocket frequently experienced hydrogen leaks.
Hydrogen leaks are difficult to manage due to the tiny molecular size of hydrogen.
The hydrogen leaks caused technical delays.
Both LH2 and LOX are constantly replenished or topped off up until shortly before launch.
LH2 and LOX are topped off to prevent pressure build-up from cryogenic fuels turning into gas.
